findings.title: Closing the Rex + Ollie element less than 0.6 s after it redraws silences its verdict on reopening: the pending live-region timer fires while it is closed and marks the verdict as already spoken
findings.location: src/app.html:892 duoPlaceholder() resets BAY.duo.spoken but leaves BAY.duo.liveTimer running; the timer is set at src/app.html:3657-3659 in renderInto
findings.evidence:
Script: reviewA2/ux/live2.js. It watches #duo-live with a MutationObserver. State {duoOpen:true, duoAction:'arm'} at 1280x900. It clicks the Collide tab, closes the element after a short wait, waits 1.5 s, reopens it, then waits 3 s.
- Closed 200 ms after the tab change: 'writes before reopening 1, all writes ["5947 Ollie hits Rex at 15.2 m/s. Rex is knock"]'. The only write lands while the element is closed, when its live region is hidden, so nothing is announced. Nothing is written after reopening, because the timer set BAY.duo.spoken to that verdict and the reopened render's verdict is the same text.
- Closed 1.5 s after the tab change: 'all writes ["6034 ...","9163 ..."]'. Reopening announces the verdict again, as intended (duoPlaceholder sets spoken = null so it is re-announced).
- So whether a screen-reader user hears the two-player result on reopening depends on how quickly they closed the element.
findings.expected: Reopening the element always announces its verdict once, in its own live region (the round 1 code-7 design: each bay announces when its verdict changes, and closing resets it).
findings.fix: Cancel the pending announcement when the element is cleared: const duoPlaceholder = () => { $('#duo-bay').replaceChildren(el('p', { class: 'muted', text: 'Working it out…' })); BAY.duo.spoken = null; clearTimeout(BAY.duo.liveTimer); };. Checked on a patched copy (reviewA2/ux/fixlive.html, live2fix.js): closed after 200 ms gives 'writes before reopening 0, all writes ["7763 Ollie hits Rex ..."]', so the verdict is announced after reopening. The 1.5 s case is unchanged.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. renderInto (src/app.html:3657-3659) sets a 600 ms timer. The timer reads `vd`, the verdict node it captured, and writes that text to #duo-live, then sets BAY.duo.spoken to it. duoPlaceholder (src/app.html:892) replaces #duo-bay's children and sets spoken = null, but it leaves that timer running. stopDuo only bumps duoGen and doesn't touch it either. If the element is closed less than about 600 ms after a redraw, the timer fires while #duo is closed. The detached `vd` still holds the verdict text, so the timer writes it to #duo-live and sets spoken to it. #duo-live sits inside the closed <details>, so it isn't rendered: checkVisibility() returns false, and assistive technology isn't told. On reopening, renderDuo draws the same verdict, the new timer finds t === B.spoken, and nothing is written. A screen-reader user hears nothing. If the user waits longer than 600 ms before closing, reopening re-announces the verdict, as round 1's code-7 intended. So whether reopening announces depends on how fast the user closed it. The defect is real, but it hits only that timing window and costs one announcement, so minor stands. Adding clearTimeout to duoPlaceholder fixes every timing I tried and leaves the slow-close case as it was.
